records.issue_text: Test mocks runQuery instead of exercising the real execution path, hiding whether real runQuery re-interpolates
records.rationale: In the newly added tests (both querySplitting.test.ts and shardQuerySplitting.test.ts), `datasource.runQuery` is spied on and stubbed to return `of({ data: [] })`, e.g. `jest.spyOn(datasource, 'runQuery').mockReturnValue(of({ data: [] }));`. This verifies only the arguments passed into `runQuery` after `applyTemplateVariables(...)` is applied, but it does not exercise the real `runQuery` implementation. If the real `runQuery` also performs its own interpolation/replacement, this test setup would not detect double-interpolation or differences in the real execution path.

records.issue_text: Repeated interpolation of the same target's expression per shard-group request in shardQuerySplitting.ts instead of interpolating once and reusing the result, which can produce incorrect expressions on later shards if template variable replacement is not idempotent
records.rationale: The diff in `shardQuerySplitting.ts` shows interpolation happening exactly once per non-hidden target during initial query collection: `request.targets ... .map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters));`. There is no code here that re-interpolates per shard-group request; it computes `queries` once and passes them to `splitQueriesByStreamShard(datasource, request, queries);`. Thus the claimed repeated interpolation "per shard-group request" in this file is contradicted by the shown code.

records.issue_text: Mock implementations of applyTemplateVariables in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:53-58 and 170-175 have arrow bodies with no return, so they return undefined instead of the query, causing tests to verify mutation side effects rather than the real API contract where the production code relies on the return value
records.rationale:
The diff shows both mocked implementations explicitly return the mutated query. E.g. in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts the mock is:
`datasource.applyTemplateVariables = jest.fn().mockImplementation((query: LokiQuery) => { ...; return query; });`
So the claim that the arrow bodies have “no return” and thus return `undefined` contradicts the diff.

records.issue_text: Assertion at shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112 changed to expect applyTemplateVariables called 5 times but only verifies the count, without asserting that each of the 5 shard queries received the interpolated expr or that shard-splitting logic operated on the interpolated selector
records.rationale: In shardQuerySplitting.test.ts, the assertion was changed from checking interpolateVariablesInQueries was called once to only checking applyTemplateVariables was called 5 times (`expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5);`). That verifies only call count, not that each of the 5 shard-generated queries actually had its `expr`/`step` interpolated, nor that shard-splitting used the interpolated selector. While other new tests assert interpolation affects the first `runQuery` call, this specific assertion is indeed weaker/less specific.
